questions.q: What is Aqabah in this lecture?
options: The stoning site in Mina near the first jamra, the location of the secret pledge
questions.explain: The Second Pledge of Aqabah was the point of no return.

questions.q: How many gathered secretly in the valley of Aqabah?
questions.explain: They gathered in the last third of the night.

questions.q: What was the Prophet's SAW answer when offered to attack the sleeping camp at Mina?
options: He refused the shortcut of violence
questions.explain: The Prophet SAW rejected the shortcut of violence.

questions.q: Why is a person's quality not measured by how long he has been Muslim?
options: Abu Jabir had been Muslim only hours yet was made a naqib
questions.explain: Quality is not measured by length of time in Islam.

questions.q: What is meant by giving an exit before the door is locked?
options: Anyone unwilling to bear the commitment is given the chance to leave
questions.explain: Be transparent about risk and give a chance to leave.

questions.q: What is the core of da'wah according to this lecture?
Each party to a pact must be clear about terms and risks with no hidden clauses.
Mature faith asks what it can give, not what it can get.
Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Gathering in the valley of Aqabah

questions.explain: Mus'ab returned, they gathered at Aqabah, Al-Abbas spoke, the pledge was taken, and twelve naqibs were appointed.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The helpers, the people of Madinah who supported the Prophet SAW
A pledge of allegiance by placing a hand in hand
Another name for the Second Pledge of Aqabah
Companions who migrated from Makkah to Madinah

questions.explain: Bay'ah is a pledge, the Ansar are the helpers, the Muhajirun are those who migrated, and Bay'at al-Harb is another name for the Second Aqabah.

questions.q: Which three short phrases make people comfortable being near us?
questions.explain: Small talk and appreciation build loyalty.
